transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. Um... I hope I’m explaining this right, but I guess I just came in because I’ve been in a bit of a... a slump, I suppose? 

It's probably nothing too major, and I really don't want to waste your time, but the things that usually make me feel like myself have just started feeling kind of flat and heavy. Like, I usually do these photography walks, and I mentor some kids in my neighborhood... and, well, I'm an executive assistant, so keeping a perfectly clean, organized calendar is sort of my pride and joy. But lately, I just... I stopped initiating any of it. 

I'm trying my best to push through and keep a good attitude, I really am, but I just haven't had the drive to start those things anymore. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information to start with.
Have you been feeling down or depressed?

I don't know if I would use the word depressed, exactly. That sounds a bit... heavy? I really don't want to make it sound worse than it actually is. 

I guess I’ve been feeling a little down, sure, but I'm still getting up and going to work every day and doing what I need to do. I just don't want you to think I'm completely falling apart or anything. It’s more just... a lack of energy for the extra stuff, I suppose. Is it okay if I just call it a funk? I hope I'm answering your question right, I just don't want to exaggerate.
Have the things you usually enjoy been less enjoyable lately?

Yeah, I... I guess that ties into what I was trying to explain earlier. I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I just want to make sure I'm giving you good answers. 

But yes, exactly. That's actually what made me come in. The things that usually make me feel like myself—like my photography walks, or mentoring the kids, even just keeping my calendar perfectly clean—they've just started feeling sort of... flat and heavy. 

It's not that I hate them now! I really don't want to sound ungrateful or anything. It's just that the spark is missing, I suppose, so I just stopped initiating them. I hope that makes sense? I'm really trying to keep a positive perspective on it, but the enjoyment just isn't quite there right now. Am I explaining that okay?
How long have you been feeling this way?

Well, um... I guess it's been a little while now. Maybe about a year and three months? Give or take. 

It really seemed to start after, well, a family member of mine had some health issues and their behavior started changing. I ended up taking on a lot more of the coordination for their care and things like that. Which I was happy to do! I really don't mind helping out my family, I want to make that clear. It's just... I think maybe taking on that extra load sort of triggered this little slump I'm in. 

I hope it doesn't sound like I'm complaining about helping my family, because I'm really not. I just want to give you the right timeline. Does that timeline sound helpful to you?
If the family situation were to improve, do you think this slump would lift?

I... I honestly don't know. I'd like to think so, you know? It would be nice if it were just a matter of the stress lifting. 

But I'm not really sure if it works that way. Even when things are relatively quiet for a few days, I still feel that same sort of... flatness. I hope that doesn't sound pessimistic! I'm really trying to stay hopeful that things will bounce back once everything settles down. I just wouldn't want to promise you that it's all tied to the family stuff and then find out I was wrong. Does that make sense? I'm just trying to be as accurate as I can for you.
Have you felt this flat or low most days for the past two years?

Oh, um, no, definitely not two years. Like I said, I really think it's just been the last year and a few months, since everything with my family started. 

Before that, I was doing really well! I was keeping on top of everything at work—I'm an executive assistant, so I have to be pretty organized—and I was really enjoying my usual routines. I wouldn't want you to think I've been dragging along for years or anything like that. I'm usually a very upbeat, capable person, I promise. It's just been this recent stretch that's been a little tougher. Does that help clarify the timeline for you? I want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need.
For most of the past year, have you felt sad or down nearly every day?

Well, um... I guess I wouldn't say *sad*, necessarily. That sounds a bit... strong, you know? 

I mean, I've definitely felt a little less energetic, maybe a bit more drained than usual. But I still get up and go to work every day, and I still take care of things for my family. I wouldn't want you to think I'm just sitting around crying all the time, because I'm definitely not! I'm still functioning and doing what I need to do. 

It's more just a... a lack of my usual spark, I suppose. Just feeling a bit flat, like I mentioned before. I hope that's the kind of answer you're looking for? I just want to make sure I'm not making it sound worse than it actually is.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Trouble sleeping? Um... well, I wouldn't really call it trouble, exactly. I hope it doesn't sound like a bad thing, but... there have definitely been nights where I only sleep, oh, maybe two or three hours? 

But the thing is, I don't feel tired at all! I'll wake up way before dawn, and instead of feeling exhausted, I just feel completely ready to go. I'll actually start answering emails or updating the executives' appointment lists. It's actually been quite productive, to be honest. I figure if my body is awake, I might as well get a head start on the day, right? 

I hope that's not a bad sign? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right idea of how things are going, and I really don't mind the extra time to get my work done. Does that make sense?
During those times when you sleep only a few hours and still feel fully energized, do you also feel unusually upbeat or irritable?

Well, um... I guess I wouldn't say irritable, really. That sounds so... difficult, you know? I really try to be easy to work with. 

But I suppose during those times, I do have these stretches where I just feel incredibly upbeat. Like, everything is just clicking perfectly, and I'm totally on top of my game. It's actually a really great feeling! 

Although... I will admit, sometimes if I'm in that zone and something tiny happens—like, if one of the executives suddenly moves a meeting without telling me—I might get just a little bit sharp with people. It actually surprises me when it happens, because I'm usually so accommodating! I just... I get so focused when I'm feeling that good, and little interruptions can be a bit frustrating. 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible person to work with? I promise I always apologize right away if I snap at anyone. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
During those energized periods, do you find yourself taking on more projects or becoming more unusually productive than is typical for you?

Well, yes, I suppose I do. But I always want to make sure I'm being as helpful as possible, you know? 

When I get into one of those really energized moods, I just... I feel like I can tackle anything. I'll start rebuilding all our office work templates, and then I'll be making care plans for my family, and emailing relatives I haven't talked to in ages, and completely reorganizing the executive files... all at the exact same time. 

It just feels like if I sit still for even a minute, I'm dropping the ball on something important. I really pride myself on being on top of things, so I just keep going and going. I hope that's okay? I mean, it's a good thing to be productive and helpful, right? I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job.
When those energized, highly productive periods happen, what is the longest they typically last?

Oh, um... how long do they last? Well, I hope it doesn't make me sound like I'm, you know, out of control or anything. I really do keep everything at the office running smoothly! But these... these elevated stretches, where I'm so driven and getting by on less sleep, and maybe feeling just a little bit too confident... they've been coming and going for about eleven months now. 

I mean, it's not eleven months straight! Just recurring on and off over that whole time. I really hope I didn't wait too long to mention it? I just figured since I was being so helpful to the executives and getting my work done, it wasn't really a problem to worry anyone about. Does that timeline make sense to you? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the right information.
What is the longest number of days in a row that one of those energized periods has lasted?

Oh, um, days in a row? Let me think... I really try not to let it get out of hand, I promise. I always make sure I'm at my desk by 8 AM sharp, no matter what. 

But, well, if I'm being completely honest... I guess the longest one stretch lasted was maybe... a week? Or maybe a week and a half? 

I hope that doesn't sound too extreme. I really was getting so much done during that time! The office never looked better, and my bosses were thrilled with how fast I was turning around their reports. It's just... after about ten days of going at that pace, I did start to feel a little bit worn out, even though my mind was still racing. 

Is a week or so a normal amount of time for something like that to last? I just want to make sure I'm not, you know, doing something wrong or letting it go on too long.
